summary: The International Nuclear Energy Act of 2025 aims to create a coordinated, whole-of-government approach for U.S. international nuclear cooperation, nuclear exports, and advanced nuclear reactor technology. The bill establishes new White House coordination offices, working groups, and grant programs to assist countries developing civil nuclear programs while promoting U.S. nuclear companies and technologies abroad.

affected_groups.effect: May benefit from increased government promotion of civil nuclear exports, participation in international advisory arrangements, and contracts funded by grants to foreign nations.
Eligible to receive financial assistance grants of up to $5.5 million per year (capped at 5 total grants per nation) and technical support to build civil nuclear energy programs.
Tasked with new reporting duties, interagency working groups, international meetings, and oversight responsibilities over a 20-year period before sunset.
affected_groups.group: Federal agencies (Department of Energy, Department of State, Department of Commerce)

key_provisions: Establishes a White House focal point (an office within the National Energy Dominance Council) to coordinate international civil nuclear cooperation and export strategy.
Creates a Nuclear Exports Working Group to establish a 10-year civil nuclear trade strategy and set biennial export targets.

Requires the Secretary of State, Secretary, and Secretary of Commerce to meet with at least 5 ally or partner nations to collaborate on advanced nuclear reactor technologies and cost-sharing arrangements.
Authorizes $15.5 million for fiscal years 2026 through 2030 for the Secretary of Energy to support the safe and peaceful use of civil nuclear technology in developing countries.
Authorizes $50 million for fiscal years 2026 through 2030 for the Secretary of State to provide grants and technical assistance to embarking civil nuclear nations.
Establishes a Strategic Infrastructure Fund Working Group to evaluate the creation of a fund supporting civil nuclear and microprocessor infrastructure projects.
Requires a joint consultative mechanism with India to discuss aligning domestic nuclear liability rules with international norms.
missing_information: Exact overall fiscal impact beyond the specific authorizations totaling $65.5 million for certain programs.
Specific details on the composition and location of the Advanced Reactor Coordination and Resource Center if established.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The International Nuclear Energy Act of 2025 aims to create a coordinated, whole-of-government approach for U.S. international nuclear cooperation, nuclear exports, and advanced nuclear reactor technology. The bill establishes new White House coordination offices, working groups, and grant programs to assist countries developing civil nuclear programs while promoting U.S. nuclear companies and technologies abroad.
summary_detail.significance: This bill sets a structured, multi-agency federal policy to advance U.S. civil nuclear technology exports and counter foreign civil nuclear influence. It impacts international diplomatic relations with partner countries and developing nuclear nations, allocates specific funding authorizations totaling $65.5 million across multiple years, and creates long-term coordination structures within the executive branch.

title: International Nuclear Energy Act of 2025
